issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor drops top-level Delimited and silently regresses mixed ADD/DROP statements
issues.detail: The prior Delimited(OneOf(...)) allowed multiple comma-separated heterogeneous alter actions in one statement; the new bare OneOf only allows one action per ALTER TABLE. A previously-valid fixture (ADD column_b ..., DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c) was deleted rather than supported. Either restore multi-action support or explicitly document the narrowing.

issues.description: Identity seed grammar represents signed numbers as two sibling nodes instead of one signed value
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar is now an optional sibling of NumericLiteralSegment rather than wrapped into a single signed-numeric value. Downstream consumers must reassemble sign+magnitude from two adjacent parse-tree nodes. Wrap in a SignedNumericLiteralSegment so the IDENTITY seed remains one value, or document the shape explicitly.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE silently accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no fixture or justification
issues.detail: The grammar widened to permit a numeric literal alongside identifier/quoted-string forms, but no test exercises the numeric branch and the PR description does not mention language-id (e.g. lcid 1033). Either cite the MS docs and add a fixture, or drop the NumericLiteralSegment alternative.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT inner Sequence makes the CONSTRAINT keyword optional, accepting invalid TSQL
issues.detail: The nested Sequence(Sequence('CONSTRAINT', IfExistsGrammar, optional=True), ObjectReferenceSegment) parses bare object references with no CONSTRAINT keyword as valid DROP targets, which TSQL does not permit. Tighten so CONSTRAINT is required on each delimited item, or flatten and document the intent.

issues.description: Four unrelated parser changes shipped as a single diff
issues.detail: Table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative identity seeds, and ALTER TABLE DROP restructuring are independent features touching different grammars. Bundling them defeats bisect when one regresses later. Split into one patch per feature, each with its own fixture.

issues.description: No literate comment marks the structural shift in AlterTableStatementSegment
issues.detail: A 160-line restructure removes the top-level Delimited and pushes delimitation inside each DROP branch, with no in-code note stating the new invariant or the deliberate scope change. One comment block above the OneOf naming the invariant would save the next maintainer significant archaeology.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The ALTER TABLE rewrite is the central concern: replacing Delimited(OneOf(...)) with a bare OneOf silently narrows the grammar and a previously-valid mixed ADD/DROP fixture was deleted rather than supported. The identity seed grammar complects sign and magnitude across two sibling nodes instead of producing one signed value. Smaller issues include an unmotivated NumericLiteralSegment in DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, an over-permissive optional CONSTRAINT keyword in DROP, four unrelated features bundled into one patch, and no literate comment marking the structural shift.
